topic_ko: 동물 체격과 시간 경험·생존 전략의 상관관계
_note: 주제(논설문) FULL set. 유형마다 passage 를 다르게 paraphrase. grammar/vocab의 밑줄 어구는 해당 passage 문장에 글자 그대로 존재. blank_target/insert_sentence 역시 해당 passage에 존재.

passage: The way animals experience time is closely linked to their body size.
Small animals need extremely fast reflexes to handle their tiny limbs and process rapid movement signals.
Because small species burn energy quickly and store very little of it, they have almost no room for flexibility in feeding, defense, or reproduction.
Moreover, short life spans give them barely any chance to learn from past experience.
For this reason, animals with short lives depend heavily on built-in behavioral routines that work without any environmental adjustment.
Large animals, on the other hand, can function well even with slower reactions and have the freedom to experiment with different mating and foraging strategies.
A longer life makes learning and memory more valuable, while reducing the importance of rigid automatic behaviors.
Furthermore, long-lived animals that travel widely are far more likely to encounter and adapt to major environmental shifts.
choices: how small animals compensate for their limited energy reserves through diet
significance of animal size in life spans and survival skills
the evolutionary origin of instinctive behaviors in mammals
why larger animals tend to have slower metabolic rates than smaller ones
the relationship between migration distance and memory capacity in birds
theme.explanation_ko: 글 전체가 체격(size)에 따라 수명과 생존 기술(반사 신경·본능적 행동·학습·기억)이 어떻게 달라지는지를 설명한다. '동물 체격이 수명과 생존 기술에서 갖는 의의'인 ②가 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ①소형 동물의 식이 보상, ③포유류 본능의 진화적 기원, ④신진대사율 차이 이유, ⑤조류 이주·기억 관계는 글의 핵심 논지가 아니다.

passage: It is not just body shape that distinguishes small animals from large ones — it is also the pace at which they experience time.
Tiny creatures must react in fractions of a second, leaving little room for reflection.
Their limited energy stores force them into rigid, predetermined patterns of behavior.
And because their lives are brief, there is almost no opportunity to accumulate knowledge from experience.
We should therefore recognize that small size pushes animals toward instinct-dominated survival strategies.
Large animals, by contrast, enjoy longer lives and slower rhythms, which allow them to update their behaviors through observation.
A long life span essentially trains animals to value learning and memory over automatic responses.
Educators and biologists should consider these size-driven differences when designing studies of animal cognition.
choices: 소형 동물은 에너지 효율을 높이기 위해 행동 다양성을 포기해야 한다.
생물 연구자들은 동물의 체격보다 신진대사율에 더 주목해야 한다.
동물의 크기가 본능 중심인지 학습 중심인지를 결정한다는 점을 인식해야 한다.
장수하는 대형 동물도 포식자 앞에서는 본능적 반사 신경에 의존한다.
동물 인지 연구는 체격이 아닌 환경 변화량을 기준으로 설계해야 한다.
claim.explanation_ko: 필자는 체격(크기)이 동물의 본능 대 학습 전략 선택을 결정한다는 점을 인식해야 한다고 주장한다. ③이 정답.
claim.distractor_ko: ①에너지 효율 포기, ②신진대사율 우선, ④포식 상황의 본능, ⑤환경 변화량 기준은 글의 핵심 주장이 아니다.

passage: Body size determines how quickly an animal experiences and responds to the world.
Small animals rely on rapid reflexes and fixed behavioral programs because their short lives and scarce energy leave little room for learning.
A one-percent difference in size can mean vastly different survival strategies — not just in speed, but in flexibility.
Large animals, with their longer lives and slower metabolisms, invest instead in learning, memory, and behavioral variation.
This is why a mouse and an elephant, facing the same challenge, solve it in fundamentally different ways.
The mouse trusts instinct; the elephant draws on experience.
Neither strategy is superior — each is perfectly suited to the animal's time scale.
In short, size shapes the fundamental balance between hardwired instinct and flexible learning.
choices: 소형 동물은 대형 동물에 비해 환경 변화에 더 잘 적응할 수 있다.
동물의 체격은 본능적 행동과 학습 행동 사이의 균형을 결정한다.
신진대사율이 높을수록 동물의 인지 능력이 뛰어난 경향이 있다.
대형 동물은 소형 동물보다 에너지 비축량이 항상 더 크다.
동물의 수명은 서식지 환경의 변화 속도에 의해 결정된다.
gist.explanation_ko: 글의 요지는 체격이 본능(사전 프로그램 행동)과 학습(유연한 행동) 사이의 균형을 결정한다는 것이다. ②가 정답.
gist.distractor_ko: ①적응력 우위는 글에 없고, ③신진대사↔인지 능력, ④에너지 비축 절대량 비교, ⑤수명 결정 요인은 모두 본문과 다른 논점이다.

passage: Time does not flow at the same rate for all animals — it compresses or expands with body size.
A shrew lives its whole life at frantic speed, relying on reflexes and instinct simply to survive each moment.
An elephant, meanwhile, moves through the world more slowly, accumulating decades of experience and memory.
Between these extremes lies every other animal, each calibrated to its own temporal scale.
Small size means brief life, scarce energy, and a near-total dependence on preprogrammed behaviors.
Large size means longer life, surplus time, and the freedom to learn from observation and error.
Neither instinct nor learning is universally superior — each suits the timescale nature assigned.
Body size, in the end, is the master dial that sets an animal's relationship with time and survival.
choices: How Instinct and Learning Compete for Dominance in the Wild
Size as the Master Dial: Time, Lifespan, and Survival Strategies
Why Small Animals Are Better Adapted to Environmental Change
The Hidden Costs of Being a Large Animal in the Modern World
Metabolic Rate as the Key Driver of Animal Behavioral Diversity
title.explanation_ko: 체격이 시간 경험·수명·생존 전략 모두를 결정하는 핵심 요소(master dial)라는 글의 핵심을 압축한 ②가 제목으로 가장 적절하다.
title.distractor_ko: ①본능↔학습 경쟁이 아닌 체격이 주제, ③소형이 환경 적응에 유리하다는 내용 없음, ④대형 동물의 비용은 부차적, ⑤신진대사율 중심은 글의 일부일 뿐이다.

passage: A telescoping of time correlates with size.
Small animals' reflexes must be quicker in order to control much smaller limbs and respond to rapid locomotor feedback.
Decision making must be streamlined in small species because their high metabolic rates and minimal energy reserves offer few choices in food-searching activities.
A short lifetime offers little time for learning from experience.
Being short-lived puts a premium on the effectiveness of preprogrammed behavior patterns that require little in the way of environmental fine-tuning.
Large animals can get by with rather slower reflexes and may have a considerable opportunity to learn by observation and trial and error.
Being longer-lived puts a greater premium on learning and memory, and less on automatic preprogrammed behaviors.
Living a long time or having the capacity to travel for long distances are more likely to expose an animal to significant changes in the environment.
choices: ①
②
③
④
⑤
grammar.explanation_ko: ⑤ or로 연결된 동명사 주어(Living a long time or having the capacity to travel)는 단수 취급 → 'is more likely'가 옳다. 'are'는 어법상 틀리다.
grammar.distractor_ko: ①in order to + 동사원형(control) 목적 부정사, ②가산 복수 choices 앞 few, ③복수 선행사 patterns를 받는 관계사절 that require, ④동명사 주어와 병렬 생략(less on~) 모두 옳다.

Small animals' reflexes must be quicker to control much smaller limbs and respond to rapid locomotor feedback.

vocab.explanation_ko: ③ 글은 소형 동물이 학습·조정 없이 즉각 작동하는 '사전 프로그램(preprogrammed)' 행동에 의존한다고 설명한다. 'expanded(확장된)'는 의미가 정반대이므로 문맥상 틀리다 → preprogrammed로 고쳐야 한다.
vocab.distractor_ko: ①correlates with(상관관계를 이루다), ②streamlined(간소화된), ④greater premium(더 높은 가치), ⑤significant(중요한)은 모두 문맥에 적절하다.

passage: The telescoping of time is directly linked to body size.
Small animals must have faster reflexes to handle their tiny limbs and process movement signals quickly.
High metabolic rates and minimal energy reserves leave small species with very few behavioral options.
And because their lives are short, there is almost no time to accumulate knowledge from experience.
As a result, being short-lived puts a premium on the effectiveness of preprogrammed behavior patterns that require little in the way of environmental fine-tuning.
Large animals, in comparison, can operate with slower reflexes and have the freedom to diversify their foraging and mating strategies.
In general, __________.

blank.explanation_ko: 앞에서 소형 동물이 사전 프로그램 행동에 의존한다고 했고 뒤에서 대형 동물의 유연한 행동을 언급하므로, 빈칸에는 '수명이 길수록 학습과 기억에 더 높은 가치를 둔다'는 내용이 자연스럽게 이어져야 한다.
blank.distractor_ko: ②에너지 비축↔행동 다양성, ③단명 동물의 사회 구조, ④반사 속도↔지능, ⑤대형 체격↔신진대사 효율은 본문의 논리와 무관하거나 반대이다.

order.given: A telescoping of time correlates with size. Small animals' reflexes must be quicker in order to control much smaller limbs and respond to rapid locomotor feedback.

blocks.A: Large animals, in comparison, can get by with rather slower reflexes, can afford to vary their mating and food-searching behaviors, and may have a considerable opportunity to learn by observation and trial and error. Being longer-lived puts a greater premium on learning and memory, and less on automatic preprogrammed behaviors.
blocks.B: Further, decision making must be streamlined in small species because their high metabolic rates and minimal energy reserves offer few choices in food-searching activities, defending against predators, or mating behaviors. And, perhaps most important, a short lifetime offers little time for learning from experience.
blocks.C: As a result, being short-lived puts a premium on the effectiveness of preprogrammed behavior patterns that require little in the way of environmental fine-tuning. In addition, living a long time or having the capacity to travel for long distances is more likely to expose an animal to significant changes in the environment.

order.explanation_ko: 주어진 글(소형 동물의 빠른 반사 신경)에 이어 (B)에서 소형 종의 의사결정 제약과 짧은 수명을 설명하고, (C)에서 그 결론(사전 프로그램 행동 중시)을 제시한 뒤, (A)에서 대형 동물 대비로 전환한다. (B)-(C)-(A).
order.distractor_ko: (A)의 대형 동물 대비가 (B)(C)의 소형 동물 설명보다 먼저 올 수 없고, (C)의 'As a result'는 (B)의 내용을 받는 결론이므로 반드시 (B) 뒤에 위치해야 한다.

passage: Body size determines how animals experience and respond to time.
Small animals require rapid reflexes and streamlined decision making because of high metabolic rates and minimal energy reserves.
Because their lives are short, they have little opportunity to learn from experience.
As a result, short-lived animals rely on preprogrammed behaviors that need minimal environmental adjustment.
Large animals can function with slower reflexes and have the freedom to diversify their behaviors.
Being longer-lived places greater value on learning and memory.
Longer life spans and wider travel ranges also expose animals to greater environmental variety.
In short, body size sets the balance between instinct and learning.
summary.summary_template: Animal body size shapes survival strategies: small, short-lived animals depend on __(A)__ behaviors requiring little environmental adjustment, while large, long-lived animals invest more in __(B)__ and memory.
summary.explanation_ko: 소형 단명 동물은 (A)preprogrammed(사전 프로그램된) 행동에 의존하고, 대형 장수 동물은 (B)learning(학습)과 기억에 더 투자한다. ①이 정답.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)는 flexible/learned/automatic이 아닌 preprogrammed, (B)는 instinct/reflexes/migration이 아닌 learning이어야 한다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 수명이 짧다는 것은 환경적 미세 조정이 거의 필요하지 않은 사전 프로그램된 행동 패턴의 효과성에 높은 가치를 둔다.
writing.answer: Being short-lived puts a premium on the effectiveness of preprogrammed behavior patterns that require little in the way of environmental fine-tuning.
writing.explanation_ko: 동명사 주어 Being short-lived + 동사 puts a premium on + 목적어 the effectiveness of preprogrammed behavior patterns + 관계절 that require little in the way of environmental fine-tuning.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 수명이 더 길다는 것은 학습과 기억에 더 높은 가치를 두고, 자동화된 사전 프로그램 행동에는 덜 중점을 둔다.
writing.answer: Being longer-lived puts a greater premium on learning and memory, and less on automatic preprogrammed behaviors.
writing.explanation_ko: 동명사 주어 Being longer-lived + puts a greater premium on A, and less on B 병렬 구조 (두 번째 puts a premium 생략).

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 대형 동물은 다소 느린 반사 신경으로도 살아갈 수 있고, 행동을 더 잘 최적화하기 위해 짝짓기 및 먹이 탐색 행동을 다양화할 여유가 있다.
conditions: can get by with를 사용할 것
in an effort to를 포함할 것
writing.answer: Large animals can get by with rather slower reflexes, can afford to vary their mating and food-searching behaviors in an effort to better optimize their behaviors.
writing.explanation_ko: can get by with + 명사(slower reflexes), can afford to + 동사원형(vary), in an effort to + 동사원형(optimize) — 목적 표현.

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: In addition, living a long time or having the capacity to travel for long distances is more likely to expose an animal to significant changes in the environment.
writing.answer: 또한, 오랫동안 살거나 장거리를 이동할 능력을 갖는 것은 동물이 환경의 중요한 변화에 노출될 가능성을 더 높인다.
writing.explanation_ko: 동명사 주어 living a long time or having the capacity(단수 is), be more likely to expose A to B(A를 B에 노출시킬 가능성이 더 높다), significant changes in the environment(환경의 중요한 변화).

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.summary: Body size determines animal survival strategies: short-lived small animals rely on (A)___________ behavior patterns, while long-lived large animals place a greater premium on (B)___________ and memory.
writing.explanation_ko: (A) 소형 단명 동물은 본문의 'preprogrammed behavior patterns'에 의존하고, (B) 대형 장수 동물은 본문의 'learning and memory'에 더 높은 가치를 둔다.

writing.context: Further, decision making must be ___________ in small species because their high metabolic rates and minimal energy reserves offer few choices in food-searching activities, defending against predators, or mating behaviors.
writing.explanation_ko: 소형 종은 에너지 제약으로 선택지가 거의 없으므로 의사결정이 '간소화(streamlined)'되어야 한다.
